bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Cabinet Clears AI Policy 2026, Offers Incentives to Draw AI Companies, GCCs and Startups
bihar_raw_news.content: artificial intelligence Bihar Cabinet Clears AI Policy 2026, Offers Incentives to Draw AI Companies, GCCs and Startups By Elets News Network - 29 October 2026 Share: Bihar has formally entered India’s race to court artificial intelligence investment. The state Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, on Wednesday, 28 October, approved the Bihar Artificial Intelligence Policy 2026 , a framework designed to bring AI companies, global capability centres (GCCs), startups and digital enterprises to the state while embedding AI deeper into how the government delivers services. The policy was among 43 proposals cleared at the Cabinet meeting, alongside a new MSME policy and a bio-fuel and compressed biogas promotion policy, signalling a wider push by the state to reposition its economy around industry and new technology. A broad incentive package for AI businesses According to Additional Chief Secretary Arvind Chaudhary and a press note from the state’s Information Technology Department, the policy offers a wide menu of financial support for eligible AI-focused units. This includes: Capital investment subsidies and interest subvention Incentives for cloud infrastructure usage Lease rental and power tariff subsidies Employment generation support, including help with ESI and EPF contributions SGST reimbursement, certification reimbursement and export incentives Specific incentives for AI model development The government has also kept room for tailor-made packages for eligible large units. The press note did not spell out incentive rates, eligibility thresholds or financial caps, which are expected to be detailed in the operational guidelines. Startups, research and infrastructure For the startup ecosystem, the policy promises incubation facilities, financial assistance, mentoring, innovation challenges and market access support. It also proposes Centres of Excellence, closer industry–academia collaboration, and help with developing and commercialising intellectual property. On the infrastructure side, Bihar plans innovation hubs, data and computing facilities, IT parks and plug-and-play spaces, and wants AI solution providers, system integrators and data service companies to set up operations in the state. AI for governance and priority sectors Governance sits at the centre of the policy. The state has identified agriculture, healthcare, education, manufacturing and urban services as priority areas where AI can improve efficiency, transparency and service delivery. Earlier drafts reviewed by the Chief Minister also flagged land reforms and disaster management as use cases. Talent is the other pillar. During a review of the draft policy, the IT Department outlined a goal to train five lakh young people in AI over five years . The state has been working with IIT Patna on an advanced IT and AI research centre and a deeptech startup lab, and has signed non-financial MoUs with technology players including Google, Microsoft, CoRover’s BharatGPT and Sarvam AI for AI capacity building among officials, teachers and youth. The government has also said it intends to hold a major annual AI conference for the next five years. Why it matters States are fast becoming a key layer of India’s AI story. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Completes Aadhaar Seeding for 95.12% of Social Security Pension Beneficiaries
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Completes Aadhaar Seeding for 95.12% of Social Security Pension Beneficiaries 29 Oct 2026 2 min read Why in News? Bihar has completed Aadhaar seeding for 1.03 crore social security pension beneficiaries , covering 95.12% of the total beneficiaries under various state and centrally sponsored pension schemes. Key Points Scheme-wise Progress: The Mukhyamantri Vridhjan Pension Yojana recorded the highest number of beneficiaries with completed Aadhaar seeding, at 54,17,180. Other schemes include: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme: 25,21,601 Laxmibai Social Security Pension Scheme: 8,71,927 Mukhyamantri Divyangjan Pension Yojana: 8,48,387 Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme: 5,58,769 Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme: 88,710. District-wise Performance: Madhubani recorded the highest number of beneficiaries with completed Aadhaar seeding among the districts highlighted in the report, with 4,95,043 beneficiaries. Other districts included Patna (approximately 4.82 lakh), East Champaran (4,77,291), Muzaffarpur (4,54,322) and Samastipur (4,35,774). Aadhaar Seeding and Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) Aadhaar Seeding: Linking Aadhaar with a beneficiary’s record in a scheme database for identification and verification. It aims to establish beneficiaries' identities, maintain accurate beneficiary records and improve transparency and efficiency in the delivery of social security pensions. Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT): DBT is a government delivery framework covering cash and in-kind benefits. Social security pensions are transferred directly to beneficiaries’ bank accounts. It was launched on 1 st January 2013. It helps reduce duplicate records, improve transparency and facilitate efficient welfare delivery. bihar_raw_news.content: Home Culture Why Bihar Museum Ranks 9th in the World, Beating New York’s Met & Other Icons Why Bihar Museum Ranks 9th in the World, Beating New York’s Met & Other Icons Patna’s Bihar Museum has ranked ninth in Worth a Journey’s 2026 list of the world’s 100 best museums, ahead of New York’s The Met and Paris’s Louvre. Here’s what to explore inside its galleries, from ancient sculptures to Bihar’s folk art. By Nishtha Kawrani Edited By Vidya Gowri Venkatesh 29 Oct 2026 Patna’s Bihar Museum has ranked ninth in Worth a Journey’s 2026 list of the world’s 100 best museums, ahead of New York’s The Met and Paris’s Louvre. Here’s what to explore inside its galleries, from ancient sculptures to Bihar’s folk art. By Nishtha Kawrani 29 Oct 2026 Follow Us New Update Bihar Museum’s ninth-place global ranking puts Patna on the map alongside some of the world’s most recognised cultural destinations. Photograph: (Instagram/@mrincoder & @aspectrum) What makes a museum worth travelling across the world for? In Patna, Bihar Museum has made a strong case for itself. It has been ranked ninth among the world’s 100 best museums in 2026, ahead of New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art, popularly known as The Met, and Paris’s Louvre. Advertisment Designed by Japanese architect Fumihiko Maki, Bihar Museum brings contemporary architecture and the state’s rich cultural heritage together. Photograph: (Instagram/ @just.adulting ) Advertisment Add The Better India As A Trusted Source Worth a Journey, an independent travel guide based in Munich, Germany, compiled the ranking using visitor reviews, data analysis, and on-site assessments. Bihar Museum is the highest-ranked museum in Asia on its list and the only Indian institution to feature in the top 100. But beyond the ranking, what can visitors expect to find here? Think ancient sculptures, archaeological treasures, folk art and contemporary architecture, all coming together to tell the story of a region whose cultural legacy stretches back centuries. Advertisment A modern space for Bihar’s ancient stories Established in 2015, Bihar Museum was created to give the state’s rich collection of historical artefacts a larger space for display. The existing Patna Museum already held a substantial collection, but a new institution offered an opportunity to present Bihar’s heritage on a much larger scale. Spread across more than 13 acres, the museum was designed by Japanese architect Fumihiko Maki, in collaboration with Mumbai-based Opolis Architects. The result is a contemporary building with expansive galleries, open courtyards and landscaped spaces that make exploring the museum an experience in itself. Ancient sculptures at Bihar Museum offer a glimpse into Bihar’s artistic traditions and centuries-old history. Photograph: (Instagram/ @patnaite ) Advertisment Inside, the exhibits take visitors through Bihar’s history, from its early civilisations to 1764. Ancient sculptures, archaeological finds, coins and manuscripts offer glimpses into the lives, beliefs and artistic traditions of people who lived here long before the modern state took shape. bihar_raw_news.title: ICAR-CIFE Kolkata Centre Organises Internship Training on Diversified Aquaculture for ...
bihar_raw_news.content: 28 October 2026, Kolkata ICAR–Central Institute of Fisheries Education, Kolkata Centre, organised a 14-day internship training programme on “Diversified Aquaculture with Best Management Practices” from 15 to 28 October 2026 for 16 Bachelor of Fisheries Science (B.F.Sc.) students specialising in Industrial Fish and Fisheries from Ramdayalu Singh (RDS) College, Muzaffarpur, Bihar. The programme familiarised students with modern aquaculture technologies, including biofloc systems, Recirculating Aquaculture Systems (RAS), aquaponics and pearl farming, along with best management practices for their effective implementation. The training also covered induced breeding and carp culture, ornamental fish breeding and culture, feeding and disease management, soil and water quality management, and fish processing. The practical sessions provided hands-on experience in induced breeding of carps, soil and water quality analysis, fish feed preparation, proximate composition analysis, pearl farming techniques and bacterial isolation. Field visits to Nalban sewage-fed aquaculture facilities and various fish farms, including an ornamental fish breeding and culture unit in Howrah, exposed the students to real-world applications of diversified aquaculture practices. The students expressed satisfaction with the training and shared positive feedback on the learning experience. The programme was conducted under the leadership of Dr. N. P. Sahu, Director, ICAR-CIFE, Mumbai, with the objective of strengthening students’ practical skills and knowledge of scientific aquaculture practices. (Source: ICAR-Central Institute of Fisheries Education, Kolkata Centre)

bihar_raw_news.title: From Patna to Kanpur, can an emerging market fix dirty, broken cities?
bihar_raw_news.content: Agencies As Patna turns to the bond market, questions remain over how Indian cities can fund better civic services Patna is preparing to borrow Rs 200 crore from the bond market, becoming the first Indian municipality to issue municipal bonds this financial year and Bihar's first-ever issuer. The proposed 10-year borrowing comes as India's cities increasingly need infrastructural renewal. Sewage spilling into rivers, rubbish piling up on streets and urban flooding repeatedly expose weak basic infrastructure. To fix that, India's cities need vastly more money than their municipal budgets can provide. But borrowing from investors is not the same as being able to repay them. A market with enormous needs and tiny volumes While Patna's issue has already been presold, Kanpur is expected to raise another Rs 125 crore in the coming months. The last municipal bond issue was Nashik's in March, while Mumbai's proposed Rs 9,500 crore offering has remained on hold amid rising yields. Also Read | Patna to raise Rs 200 crore via municipal bonds Live Events The numbers explain the gap between ambition and reality. According to the World Bank , India needs about $840 billion in urban infrastructure investment over 15 years to 2036, or roughly $55 billion annually. Its 2022 assessment found that central and state governments financed more than 75% of city infrastructure, while urban local bodies contributed around 15% through their own surplus revenues. SEBI's municipal bond data recorded 22 municipal corporations raising Rs 4,540 crore through 31 issuances as of March 31, 2026. That is a small pool of capital against the scale of India's needs. Reuters reported in May that seven to 10 new municipal issuers could enter the market in 2026-27, with a pipeline of at least Rs 4,000 crore. That would be significant progress, but hardly a revolutionary trend. What bonds can actually fix Municipal bonds allow cities to raise long-term money for projects such as water supply, sewage treatment, drainage, roads and public transport. Instead of waiting for annual government allocations, a municipality can mobilise funds upfront and spread repayment over several years. A city could finance a sewage-treatment plant today rather than build it in disconnected stages as grants arrive. A properly structured bond can also impose financial discipline as investors and rating agencies demand audited accounts, predictable revenues and clarity about repayment. But bonds are debt, not free money. A Rs 200 crore issue cannot automatically pay for Patna's entire urban renewal. Its impact depends on which projects receive funding, whether construction is completed on time and whether the resulting services are maintained. A new drainage system is of little use if drains remain clogged because the municipality cannot fund routine cleaning. bihar_raw_news.content: Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu. (File Photo |PTI) Delhi Govt sends Delhi-Bihar bus service proposal to Sandhu The Delhi government had earlier announced the project, which is part of the next phase of the rollout of the inter-state buses, with Delhi and Bihar approving the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU). Express News Service Updated: 29th Oct, 2026 at 8:20 AM NEW DELHI: Moving ahead with its plan to start inter-state buses to Bihar, the Delhi Transport Department has sent its proposal to Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu for final approval, officials said on Wednesday. The Delhi government had earlier announced the project, which is part of the next phase of the rollout of the inter-state buses, with Delhi and Bihar approving the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU). “We have a target to launch these buses before the Chhath festival this year; these will be AC luxury buses, and initially we plan to roll out over 50 buses to seven locations in Bihar. We have sent the proposal for approval to Sandhu; hopefully it will be approved soon,” Delhi Transport Minister Pankaj Singh said. Earlier, the Transport Department had announced that the buses will connect Patna, Gaya, Muzaffarpur, Darbhanga, Purnia, and Bhagalpur in Bihar with Delhi. The government believes that this initiative will not only benefit passengers but also contribute to an increase in the Delhi Transport Corporation’s (DTC’s) revenue, the officials said. According to officials, Volvo buses would ply on these longer routes as electric buses would not be a feasible option for now; depending on the response, the number of buses could also be increased. “The long-route buses will be 12 metres long, air-conditioned, and equipped with luggage space. It is not feasible to ply electric buses to far-off locations because of the lack of charging infrastructure,” an official privy to the matter revealed. Not first such service This is not the first such service. The government had earlier announced inter-state buses to Rishikesh, Haridwar and Dehradun in Uttarakhand; Panipat in Haryana; Ayodhya, Lucknow and Moradabad in Uttar Pradesh; and Amritsar, Chandigarh and Jammu. The museum showcases Bihar's history, archaeological collections and regional folk traditions. The institution also ranked first in Asia, according to the travel guide's latest assessment. The ranking covers museums dedicated to art, history, science, technology and open-air heritage. Mexico City's Museo Nacional de Antropología topped the global list, followed by Madrid's Museo del Prado in second place and Denmark's Louisiana Museum of Modern Art in third. The State Hermitage Museum in St Petersburg ranked fourth, followed by Vienna's Kunsthistorisches Museum in fifth and Turkey's Şanlıurfa Archaeology Museum in sixth. The World War II museums in Gdańsk, Poland, and New Orleans, the US, occupied seventh and eighth positions, respectively. Bihar Museum placed ahead of New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art, popularly known as The Met, which ranked tenth. According to Worth a Journey, Bihar Museum preserves the history of Bihar from the Stone Age to the modern era. Its collections include ancient sculptures , rare coins, manuscripts and folk art, alongside contemporary architectural spaces, open courtyards and landscaped grounds. Collections and visitor experience The museum's ancient sculpture galleries form a central part of its historical collection , showcasing artefacts associated with the region's past. Its regional folk art gallery highlights Bihar's diverse artistic traditions, while a dedicated children's gallery aims to make history and culture accessible to younger visitors. The children's gallery distinguishes the museum's visitor offering by providing an educational space designed specifically for young audiences and families. According to the report, this approach reflects an effort to make cultural heritage accessible beyond visitors primarily interested in ancient artefacts and artistic masterpieces. The recognition places Bihar Museum among the institutions featured in the international ranking and brings attention to Patna's cultural tourism offering. Its collections and visitor facilities provide opportunities to explore Bihar's archaeological heritage , regional art and historical development. Comments What are your thoughts?

bihar_raw_news.title: Aisshpra Gems & Jewels Expands Network to 20 Stores, Targets 30 by March 2028
bihar_raw_news.content: Aisshpra Gems & Jewels Expands Network to 20 Stores, Targets 30 by March 2028 The jewellery retailer opened four franchise showrooms in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, adding 12,000 sq. ft. of retail space and taking its total footprint beyond 90,000 sq. ft. Post By : IJ News Service On 29 October 2026 11:09 AM Aisshpra Gems & Jewels opened four franchise showrooms in Bahraich, Bettiah, Lucknow and Mirzapur on October 23, 2026, taking its operational network from 16 to 20 stores. The Gorakhpur-based jewellery retailer aims to expand to 30 stores by March 2028, with three additional showrooms currently under construction. Each of the four new showrooms measures approximately 3,000 sq. ft., adding around 12,000 sq. ft. to the company’s retail footprint, which now exceeds 90,000 sq. ft. The Bettiah showroom marks the brand’s entry into Bihar, with Siwan and Gopalganj identified as potential expansion markets. The Lucknow opening takes its presence in the city to three showrooms. All four locations feature a dedicated store-in-store format for Jewel Story, Aisshpra’s lifestyle jewellery brand. The concept targets teenagers, young adults and consumers up to around 40 years of age, offering lightweight, contemporary jewellery in 9KT to 22KT gold. The range is positioned for everyday wear alongside the retailer’s traditional, bridal and occasion-wear collections. The inaugurations were attended by actor Mouni Roy in Lucknow, Adah Sharma in Bahraich and Ayesha Khan in Mirzapur. The Bettiah showroom was inaugurated in the presence of local dignitaries. Founded in Gorakhpur in 1940, Aisshpra Gems & Jewels offers gold, diamond and silver jewellery. Its expansion strategy combines franchise-led retail growth with the development of lifestyle jewellery offerings aimed at younger consumers. bihar_raw_news.title: Delhi Plans Luxury Bus Services to Bihar for Chhath Puja | The CSR Journal
bihar_raw_news.content: Delhi Government Proposes Luxury Bus Services to Bihar for Chhath Puja 2026 Delhi Top Stories Transport Published By - Pooja Shah October 29, 2026 Reading time - 2 min. Facebook X Copy URL WhatsApp The Delhi government is set to introduce direct luxury bus services to Bihar ahead of Chhath Puja 2026. The Transport Department has proposed the operation of over 50 air-conditioned buses to seven destinations in Bihar, pending final approval from Lieutenant Governor TS Sandhu. This initiative aims to facilitate travel for devotees during the festival. Transport Minister Pankaj Singh announced that the proposal has been submitted for the Lieutenant Governor’s approval. The government is keen on launching these services before the Chhath festival, which is celebrated with great fervour in Bihar and among the Bihari diaspora. An agreement for interstate operations between the Delhi and Bihar governments has already been established. Singh expressed optimism regarding the approval process, stating, “We have a target to launch these buses before the Chhath festival this year; these will be AC luxury buses, and initially we plan to roll out over 50 buses to seven locations in Bihar.” Destinations and Bus Specifications The proposed bus network will connect Delhi with major cities in Bihar, including Patna, Gaya, and Muzaffarpur. The buses will be 12 metres long and comply with BS-VI emission standards, ensuring an environmentally friendly travel option. This initiative is particularly significant as it aims to improve travel options during the Chhath festival, a time when many people travel to their hometowns. Electric buses have been deemed impractical for these long routes due to inadequate charging infrastructure. Therefore, the decision to utilise air-conditioned Volvo buses is seen as a necessary measure to accommodate the expected surge in passenger demand during the festival. In addition to enhancing connectivity, the introduction of these buses is expected to provide a comfortable travel experience for passengers. The government aims to ensure that the services are reliable and efficient, catering to the needs of the travelling public during this festive season. Operational Model and Future Expansion Plans The operational model for these bus services will follow a wet-lease arrangement, whereby a private operator will manage the buses on behalf of the Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC). This model is anticipated to improve connectivity while also contributing to the revenue of the DTC. Further details regarding fare structures, departure points, booking methods, and the frequency of services are still under discussion. The Bihar initiative is part of a broader strategy for inter-state expansion, which may include additional routes to popular destinations such as Rishikesh, Haridwar, and Amritsar. As preparations for Chhath Puja continue, the Delhi government is focused on ensuring that the transport services are ready to meet the needs of the public. The success of this initiative could pave the way for more extensive inter-state bus services in the future, enhancing travel options for residents and visitors alike. bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar MSME Policy 2026 Targets 1 Crore Entrepreneurial Families Breaking News Bihar MSME Policy 2026 Targets 1 Crore Entrepreneurial Families By Ananya Sharma October 29, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp The Bihar cabinet has approved the Bihar MSME Policy 2026, targeting the creation of one crore entrepreneurial families and one crore direct and indirect jobs over the next five years. The policy is intended to strengthen the state’s economic base by improving access to finance, markets, skills and technology. The cabinet approved the detailed framework on Wednesday under the chairmanship of Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary. Cabinet Secretariat Department Additional Chief Secretary Arwind Kumar Choudhary said the policy’s motto is ‘Ek crore udyami parivar, sashakt Bihar ka aadhar’, or one crore entrepreneurial families as the foundation of a strong Bihar. The policy seeks to raise Bihar’s credit-deposit ratio to 75% from its current level of slightly over 60%. It provides for an MSME corpus and growth fund to improve access to finance for entrepreneurs. An MSME centre will also be established in each of the state’s 38 districts. The framework identifies 10 pillars of economic activity. These include promotion of the informal economy, skill upgradation, cluster-based development, access to the MSME corpus fund and markets, emerging sectors, cooperatives, technology and environmental sustainability. The cabinet also approved a proposal from the water resources department to sign a memorandum of understanding with the National Institute of Hydrology, Roorkee, for delineating floodplain zones along the Ganga’s major tributaries in Bihar. The study will cover the Kosi, Gandak and Sone rivers, with Rs 1.99 crore sanctioned for the work. A separate emergency plan to assess the condition and safety of identified embankments across the state was also approved. The Rs 8.32-crore exercise is to be completed within eight months of commencement. It will include possible inundation maps based on dam-break analysis, emergency action plans for individual embankments and coordination arrangements between district administrations and disaster management agencies. An operation and maintenance manual will also be prepared. The cabinet approved the expansion of the Sonepur project area to accommodate proposed national and state-level projects. The existing mega Sonepur plan includes a greenfield satellite township, an international greenfield airport, a film city, educational institutions and other development projects. It also approved lifting the ban on the sale, purchase and transfer of land within the project areas of 11 proposed satellite townships. Once the township development plans are notified, construction, land development and land use in these areas will be governed by the respective plans. In aviation-related decisions, the cabinet approved a 30-year lease of 1,000 square metres of land at Saharsa airport to G R D Air Academy Private Limited for a flight training organisation and related activities. It also sanctioned Rs 43.50 crore under the viability gap funding scheme to promote the UDAN regional connectivity programme. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Plans Signature Roads Across All Cities as Urban Growth Accelerates
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar Plans Signature Roads Across All Cities as Urban Growth Accelerates Breaking News Bihar Plans Signature Roads Across All Cities as Urban Growth Accelerates By Harpreet Singh October 29, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Bihar plans to develop signature roads across all its cities as the state prepares for faster urbanisation, urban development and housing minister Nitish Mishra said on Wednesday. The proposed roads are part of a wider focus on modern infrastructure, planned growth, improved connectivity and the use of technology in public works. Mishra made the announcement while addressing the valedictory session of a 28-day training programme for junior engineers at the Lalit Narayan Mishra Institute of Economic Development and Social Change. He said infrastructure planning would become increasingly important as Bihar’s urban population expands. According to the minister, around 11% of Bihar’s population currently lives in urban areas, compared with a national average of 33%. He cited the gap while stressing the need to prepare cities for future growth through planned development rather than isolated infrastructure projects. The minister asked engineers to prioritise quality, timely execution and proper planning while delivering urban projects. He also emphasised the use of modern technology and said infrastructure should improve connectivity and the quality of life for residents. The announcement did not specify the cities to be covered, the length or design standards of the proposed signature roads, the funding arrangement, or a construction timetable. Mishra also referred to initiatives such as satellite townships, placing the proposed road programme in the context of a broader effort to manage urban expansion. Better road connectivity would be an important component of such growth, although the minister did not provide details of how the roads would connect with existing networks or planned townships. The minister further highlighted the importance of project monitoring, report writing, documentation and improved working practices among engineers. These administrative functions are intended to support project execution and oversight, particularly as the state expands its urban infrastructure programme. N Vijayalakshmi, additional chief secretary of the planning and development department, called for responsible use of public funds and transparent financial management. She also encouraged officials to adopt emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, in government work. Mishra referred to the recent All India Urban Conclave in Bhubaneswar, attended by ministers, secretaries and urban development officials from across the country. He said such forums provide opportunities for state officials to study new ideas and practices in urban development. The minister later distributed certificates to the trainees and encouraged them to undertake projects that create a lasting impact on urban development. Further details on the proposed signature roads, including locations, approvals, budgets and implementation schedules, were not announced at the programme. national_raw_news.title: World Stroke Day: Nadda Urges Citizens to Recognise Stroke Warning Signs
national_raw_news.content: World Stroke Day is being observed today to raise awareness about stroke and the importance of recognising its warning signs. This year’s campaign message, ‘Every Minute Counts – Know the Signs of Stroke’, reminds everyone that timely action can save lives. On the occasion, Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Jagat Prakash Nadda said, sudden facial drooping, weakness in an arm, or difficulty speaking should never be ignored. He emphasised that seeking immediate medical attention can make a crucial difference in recovery. He urged citizens to learn the warning signs, spread awareness, and encourage everyone to act quickly, as every minute matters. Talking to Akashvani News, Chief of the Neurosciences Centre at All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi, Dr Shailesh B Gaikwad said, stroke is a serious neurological emergency in which the blood supply to part of the brain is interrupted or a blood vessel in the brain ruptures. He said, with around 18 lakh stroke cases recorded across India each year, awareness can save lives. He added that the symptoms of the stroke include sudden loss or blurring of vision, double vision, loss of balance, and difficulty in walking. Dr Gaikwad emphasized if such symptoms are visible then the patients should immediately transfer to stroke ready hospital for treatment. Dr Gaikwad further added that high blood pressure is one of the leading risk factors for stroke. He added that other factors include diabetes, high cholesterol, certain heart conditions, smoking, excessive alcohol consumption, obesity, physical inactivity, and an unhealthy diet. Dr gaikwad informed that the risk increases with age, but stroke can occur at any age. He advised regular health check-ups and proper control of these risk factors.

national_raw_news.content: The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Ministry of Education and UNESCO today exchanged a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to take clean sport values to classrooms across India through the ‘Sports Values in Every Classroom Toolkit’. The MoU was exchanged in the presence of Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya, Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi, Director of UNESCO’s Regional Office for South Asia, Dr Tim Curtis. national_raw_news.title: Union Cabinet approves 3% hike in Dearness Allowance for central government employees
national_raw_news.content: The Union Cabinet has approved the Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme to promote domestic manufacturing.The total outlay for the scheme is ten thousand crore rupees for 13 years upto Financial Year 2039-40. The scheme aims to establish a globally competitive container manufacturing ecosystem in India, reduce import dependence and strengthen supply chain resilience. Briefing media after the Union Cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that the scheme is intended to support new manufacturing facilities as well as expansion of existing container manufacturing units. He said, it has four components including Interest Subvention Assistance, Testing and Certification assistance, Land Leasing support and Operational Expenditure Assistance. Mr Vaishnaw added that the scheme will create an internationally competitive manufacturing base, with potential to position India as a global export hub for quality shipping containers. The Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme will strengthen resilience of India’s maritime and logistics supply chains. It will generate an estimated 3,000 direct jobs and over 50,000 indirect jobs, while supporting ancillary industries such as corner castings, specialised steel, wooden frames and paints. Mr Vaishnaw informed that Union Cabinet also approved three percent increase in Dearness Allowance to Central Government employees and Dearness Relief to Pensioners with effect from 1st of July,2026. Mr Vaishnaw added that this will benefit over 48 lakh Central Government employees and 68 lakh pensioners. The Union Cabinet has also approved the Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme to position India as a global hub for high-quality sports goods. Giving details about the scheme , Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that that the scheme has an approved outlay of over one thousand 856 crore rupees over eight years period from 2026-27 to 2033-34. He said, the scheme will support the development of a globally competitive sports goods industry and strengthen India’s position in global supply chains. Mr Vaishnaw said that the Scheme envisages the development of dedicated Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones (SGMZs) to promote cluster-based manufacturing and create integrated industrial ecosystems. Mr Vaishnaw added that incentives and interventions are the two parts of the scheme where incentive supports manufacturing while intervetion builds the wider ecosystem. The Union Minister also said that a key focus of the Scheme is to attract new investments and strengthen domestic manufacturing capacity in the sports goods sector. The Anchor Investment Support component will encourage leading domestic and global manufacturers, brands and retail chains to establish manufacturing facilities within designated Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones and foster the development of robust supplier and ancillary ecosystems. Complementing this, the Turnover Linked Support component will incentivise higher production, capacity expansion and sustained manufacturing growth. Mr Vaishnaw also informed that the Union Cabinet has approved the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana (PMVGSY) scheme as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme. It aims to transform Panchayats into empowered, self-reliant, accountable and high-performing institutions of local self-government, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat. Mr Vaishnaw said that the scheme has a total financial outlay of 7,395 crore rupees and the duration of the scheme is for five years from 2026-27 to 2030-31. He said, the scheme applies to all States and Union Territories, including rural local governance institutions in non-Part IX areas where Panchayats do not exist. It will cover more than 2.78 lakh Rural Local Bodies and Traditional Bodies across the country. Mr Vaishnaw said, around 32 lakh elected representatives, along with Panchayat functionaries and other stakeholders, across over 2.55 lakh Panchayats and Traditional Local Bodies will be direct beneficiaries of the scheme. The combined impact on the exchequer on account of increase in both Dearness Allowance and Dearness Relief would be over 10,000 crore rupees per annum.

national_raw_news.title: Cyclone Arnab damages over 80,000 hectares of crops in Andhra Pradesh
national_raw_news.content: Cyclone Arnab has caused extensive damage to crops, houses, roads and power infrastructure across several districts of Andhra Pradesh. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has requested the Centre to send an inter-ministerial team for an early assessment of the losses. The State Government has intensified relief and restoration operations in the affected areas. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu reviewed cyclone relief operations through the State’s Real-Time Governance Centre and directed officials to expedite restoration of essential services. The Chief Minister announced an ex-gratia of five lakh rupees each to the families of those who lost their lives and financial assistance to affected households. Preliminary estimates indicate damage to over 70 thousand hectares of paddy and more than 10 thousand hectares of horticultural crops. Over 28 thousand people have been evacuated to relief shelters, with NDRF and SDRF teams deployed across affected districts. Electricity restoration is progressing, with nearly 80 percent of power supply restored in Visakhapatnam district. Repair work is continuing in Konaseema, Kakinada and the Godavari districts, where fallen trees and damaged electricity poles disrupted services. Officials are also clearing blocked roads and restoring drinking water supplies. Meanwhile, the Chief Minister has requested Centre to send a team to assess cyclone-related losses.

national_raw_news.title: US Federal Reserve keeps its key interest rate unchanged at 3.9% despite high inflation
national_raw_news.content: The US Federal Reserve kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at a target range of 3.75 per cent to 4.00 per cent, keeping the average effective rate at approximately 3.9 per cent despite stubbornly high inflation. In a statement released after its two-day policy meeting, the Fed said, inflation remains elevated and holding off on an increase will allow the accumulation of more information that will help determine what policy the Fed should pursue to ensure a timely return of inflation to the central bank’s 2 per cent target. The statement leaves the Fed’s next moves unclear, even though officials last month pencilled in another rate hike for this year. The Fed’s decision comes just six days before a midterm election that has focused heavily on concerns around the cost of living and affordability. Two Fed officials dissented from yesterday’s decision, with Fed governor Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack voting in favour of hiking rates by a quarter point. Consumers have generally soured on an economy weighed down by more expensive gas, groceries, and clothing, among other items. Yet Warsh faces plenty of challenges in getting inflation back to target. Other parts of the economy are already being hit by higher rates, which were lifted by market forces, even before the Fed hiked last month. Inflation picked up in September, when consumer prices rose 3.7 per cent compared with a year earlier. The increase was much bigger than the 2.4 per cent rate in February, just before the Iran war. The Fed, led by Chairman Kevin Warsh, raised its benchmark rate last month for the first time in three years, defying President Donald Trump’s demands for rate cuts. President Trump has also slammed the Fed for raising its key rate last month, though he largely blamed the central bank’s rate-setting committee, rather than Warsh, whom he appointed. Many economists argue that solid growth is evidence that interest rates aren’t particularly high and the economy could withstand higher rates to combat inflation.

Pivotal to economic growth and public welfare, these projects, were reviewed with a foc...
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi chaired the 54th meeting of PRAGATI, the ICT-enabled, multi-modal platform aimed at fostering Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation, at Seva Teerth in New Delhi yesterday. During the meeting, the Prime Minister reviewed infrastructure projects across the Railways, Ekta Malls and Drug Parks worth over 16 thousand crore rupees covering 31 States and Union Territories. Pivotal to economic growth and public welfare, these projects, were reviewed with a focus on timeliness, inter-agency coordination, and timely issue resolution. Prime Minister asked the concerned Ministries and State Governments to resolve bottlenecks in mission mode, strengthen Centre-State and inter-agency coordination, and ensure close monitoring at the senior-most level. Calling for a proactive work culture with greater ownership at every level, he stressed the need to anticipate implementation challenges, take timely decisions and fix clear accountability for completing projects on schedule. Prime Minister Modi also asked Chief Secretaries to review schemes with District Magistrates every month to address implementation gaps and ensure that benefits reach eligible beneficiaries on time. He emphasised that governance must focus on outcomes over outlays, ensuring that public expenditure translates into tangible improvements in people’s lives. Prime Minister Modi stressed that PM Ekta Malls should provide markets for local products, strengthen the livelihoods of artisans and help them expand their enterprises. He emphasised the need for regular review of progress by Chief Secretaries and to ensure timely completion of the malls. Reviewing Bulk Drug Parks in Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat and Himachal Pradesh, Mr Modi stressed the need to prioritise domestic production of active pharmaceutical ingredients and essential inputs to strengthen self-reliance. Referring to the Aspirational Districts and Aspirational Blocks Programmes, Mr Modi highlighted the role of convergence, regular monitoring and local accountability in accelerating development in underserved areas. He noted that sustained efforts to strengthen governance and improve the delivery of welfare schemes had helped nearly 25 crore people move out of multidimensional poverty. During the review of the redevelopment of Ahmedabad railway station, Mr Modi called for expediting the redevelopment of major railway stations across the country to improve passenger convenience and ease of travel. He emphasised that redeveloped stations should serve as multimodal transport hubs, with seamless connectivity to metro and other transport networks.

Excelsior Correspondent JAMMU, Oct 28: A one-day workshop on vigilance awareness for employees of CBC and the Press Information Bureau (PIB) organized by the Central Bureau of Communication (CBC) was held here today. The workshop was organized on the theme "Probity for Prosperity", emphasizing the importance of integrity, transparency and accountability in public administration. Speaking on the occasion, Director, CBC/PIB Jammu, Neha Jalali highlighted the importance of honesty, transparency and accountability in the discharge of official duties. She stressed that integrity and ethical conduct must be reflected in day-to-day official dealings and that public servants should perform their responsibilities with a strong sense of duty, fairness and commitment to public service. Deputy Superintendent, Anti-Corruption Bureau, Kamal Sangra raised awareness about various aspects of corruption, its adverse impact on public administration and the importance of vigilance in preventing corrupt practices. He also explained the circumstances and considerations that led to the introduction of the Public Interest Disclosure and Protection of Informers (PIDPI) Resolution, which provides a mechanism for reporting allegations of corruption and protecting the identity of persons making such disclosures, subject to the prescribed procedure. The participants were briefed on the scope and applicability of the resolution, including the distinction between its applicability to Central Government employees and its non-applicability to State Government employees under the framework discussed. Senior Accounts Officer CBC, Rajesh Malik; Administrative Officer, O P Maurya; Media and Communication Officer PIB, Muzafar Wani and other employees of CBC and PIB Jammu attended the workshop. national_raw_news.content: Special Campaign 6.0: Pharmaceuticals Department conducts 14,700 cleanliness drives, generates ₹2.30 lakh from scrap disposal Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Special Campaign 6.0: Pharmaceuticals Department conducts 14,700 cleanliness drives, generates ₹2.30 lakh from scrap disposal ANI | Updated: Oct 29, 2026 01:07 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 29 (ANI): The Department of Pharmaceuticals , under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilisers, along with its attached office, the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority, and associated organisations including seven NIPERs, the PMBI, and three public sector undertakings namely BCPL, HAL, and KAPL, is actively participating in the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters 6.0. Being conducted from October 2 to October 31, the campaign focuses on promoting cleanliness, scientific management and disposal of e-waste, systematic record management, effective grievance redressal, and optimum utilisation of office space, to enhance administrative efficiency and promote a clean, organised, and productive work environment. Across field and outstation offices, 14,700 cleanliness drives have been conducted so far against a baseline target of 12,208, reflecting the Department’s continued efforts to improve workplace hygiene and sanitation, strengthen environmental awareness, and foster sustainable workplace practices, an official release stated. The campaign has strengthened systematic record management and promoted the efficient utilisation of office space. Against a baseline target of 2,716 physical files and 20 e-files, the Department has reviewed 4,283 physical files and 20 e-files, while 489 files have been weeded out and closed. Additionally, 2,200 square feet of office space has been freed up through these efforts, contributing to better space management and the creation of more organised, efficient, and clutter-free workplaces. Administrative efficiency and responsive governance are being strengthened through the timely resolution of pending matters, including MP references (3 against a target of 4), parliamentary assurances(1 out of 2), a Cabinet proposal (02 proposals), State references (57 against 58) and PMO references (02 cases). Against the target of 72 public grievances and 28 appeals registered on the Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS), 132 public grievance cases and 39 appeals have been settled. Against a target of 20 items identified for easing of rules/processes, this has been completed for 17 items. These efforts aim to expedite the resolution of pending matters, improve service delivery, and promote greater accountability and efficiency in public administration. The Ministry of Chemicals also mentioned that scientific e-waste management is one of the key focus areas of SCDPM 6. The Department has targeted 1,011 obsolete electronic and electrical items - comprising IT equipment, consumer electronics, appliances, and laboratory tools - for safe disposal through empanelled recyclers under the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022. The process for disposing of these items is currently underway. Further, the Department has earned revenue of Rs 2,30,187/- from the disposal of office scrap. Department of Pharmaceuticals remains committed to the objectives of SCDPM 6 and is monitoring targets closely and documenting achievements via the National Special Campaign Portal, the release stated. (AI-generated image used for representational purpose.) AI Quick Read The Union Cabinet has approved a 3-percentage-point increase in Dearness Allowance (DA) for central government employees and Dearness Relief (DR) for pensioners, Union Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced on 28 October 2026. The decision will benefit around 48.54 lakh central government employees and 68.71 lakh pensioners. Calling the increase a Diwali gift from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Vaishnaw said the Cabinet had approved the revision at its meeting on Wednesday. According to the Press Information Bureau (PIB), the revised rates will be effective from 1 July 2026. The hike takes DA and DR from 60% to 63% of basic pay and pension, respectively. The combined annual impact on the government exchequer is estimated at ₹ 10,016.10 crore, according to the official announcement. The increase follows the accepted formula based on the recommendations of the 7th Central Pay Commission. How much will central government employees gain from the 3% DA hike? The additional amount employees receive will depend on their basic pay. A 3-percentage-point increase in DA translates into an additional 3% of basic pay every month. For instance, an employee drawing basic pay of ₹ 18,000 will receive an additional ₹ 540 per month. For an employee with basic pay of ₹ 25,000, the monthly increase will be ₹ 750. Someone with basic pay of ₹ 50,000 will receive an additional ₹ 1,500 per month. Adhil Shetty, CEO of BankBazaar, said the increase follows the established formula linked to inflation data under the 7th Pay Commission. “At Level 3 and Level 8, basic pay of ₹ 21,700 and ₹ 47,600 respectively, the increase adds ₹ 651 and ₹ 1,428 a month, with arrears due separately,” Shetty said. He added that employees could use the additional income to strengthen their savings rather than absorb it into everyday spending. “What matters next is where that money goes. Channeled into a recurring deposit, an SIP, or an emergency fund rather than daily spending, even a modest hike can gradually build into meaningful savings over time,” he said. DA is intended to help government employees offset the impact of inflation on household expenses. The Centre typically revises the allowance twice a year, with changes effective from January and July. How much more pension will retirees receive after the DR hike?
